chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever upon whom a sacrifice (hady) is obligated while in his state of Ihram, for him is that he may slaughter it wherever he wishes,
except for the ransoming of the hunted prey,
for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'an offering to be brought to the Kabah'.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فِدَاءَ: Compensation or ransom for a religious obligation or prohibition
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by a pilgrim

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter the sacrifice for hunting game during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the geographical jurisdiction for slaughtering the sacrificial animal (hady) during Hajj, distinguishing between general vows and specific compensation for hunting. While the pilgrim generally retains the freedom to slaughter the animal anywhere, the exception for fidyah requires the offering to reach the Kaaba, a ruling derived directly from the Quranic phrase 'hady reaching the Kaaba.' This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the literal and contextual interpretation of Quranic injunctions within fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhamamd, from one of his men, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The one in his Ihraam, upon whom a sacrifice is Obligated, so for him is that he should sacrifice wherever he so desires to, except for the ransoming of the hunted prey, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [5:95] an offering to be brought to the Kabah’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad certain persons of his people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who owes to offer an offering because of violation of rules in the state of Ihram can slaughter wherever he wants
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, . . an offering and ransom that must reach al-Ka‘bah.” ( 5 : 95 )’”
